name: Townhomes
summary: Attached 2–3 story wood-frame townhouses, for sale or rent. Shared party walls save exterior envelope and lot area. Rated fire separations, more stairs and higher kitchen/bath density per SF offset part of that, so per-SF cost is close to detached homes. National data is indirect: Census sale prices for attached homes, translated with NAHB cost shares. The only direct cost points are permit valuations and a builder survey from Washington State. Confidence is medium.

typicalSize.method: Units per project. A judgment: small infill rows of 6–12 units (see the Snohomish County permits in e4, 6–10 units per building) up to master-planned townhome sections of 100+.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Census 2025 attached new homes sold: median 1,824 SF, average 1,948 SF (e2). Snohomish County permits give 1,456–2,071 SF/unit (e4). BIAW reports a 1,568 SF WA average (e5). Mid ≈ the Census median, rounded.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Gross density with private drives and guest parking. A judgment: a 20–24 ft wide unit on a ~1,500–2,500 SF lot gives ~17–25 net du/ac. ~40% for drives, open space and detention gives ~10–15 gross.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Tuck-under or attached 1–2 car garage plus guest stalls. Common suburban zoning; not sourced.

perPrimaryUnit.method: = perSF × sfPerPrimaryUnit: mid $150 × 1,800 = $270k; low $115 × 1,400 ≈ $160k; high $200 × 2,200 = $440k. Cross-check: Snohomish County (WA-Seattle) 2025 permit valuations run $275k–$374k per unit (e4).

perSF.method: National anchor: Census 2025 attached homes sold at a median $165.59/SF excluding lot (e1). Times the NAHB construction share of non-lot price (0.746, see single-family e1/e9) = $123.5/SF incl. fees, or ≈ $116/SF net of fees: the builder direct cost for a typical production townhome. Add ~10% GC/OH&P for a contractor price ≈ $128. WA evidence: Snohomish County permit valuations $180–189/SF (e4, Seattle metro, where costs run roughly 15–25% above national) and the BIAW builder survey at $404/SF (e5, outlier; likely includes items beyond hard cost). Mid $150 sits between the national derived figure (~$128) and the regionalized WA permit figure (~$155), slightly above the single-family mid ($145) to reflect rated party walls and more stairs per SF. Low = the Census-derived direct cost. High = high-cost metros and premium finishes. The NAHB construction-share conversion is borrowed from detached homes (see the derivation in single-family.json).

scope.notes: Contractor price for the buildings, attached/tuck-under garages and typical on-site work (private drives, guest parking, utilities within the property, landscaping) incl. GC general conditions and OH&P. Excludes land, off-site improvements, impact/tap fees, A&E, financing, marketing/sales and FF&E.

qualityTiers.method: Low/mid of the per-SF range (115/150 ≈ 0.77, rounded to 0.8). Premium and luxury follow the single-family tiers (urban luxury townhomes with elevators and rooftop decks reach $240+/SF). Judgment.

systemSplit.method: Starts from the single-family split (NAHB 2024 Table 1 mapped to CSI). Adjustments, all judgment: 03 slightly lower (shared foundations); 07 and 09 up (rated party-wall assemblies, more gypsum layers); 22 and 26 up (more fixtures/circuits per SF in smaller units); 21 at 1% for NFPA 13D/13R sprinklers, which many jurisdictions require in attached product; 31 and 32 down (smaller lots), with 33 added for shared on-site utility mains.

lineItems.name: Residential fire sprinklers (NFPA 13D/13R)

cost.method: Set to equal the 1% Div 21 share of the systemSplit at ~$150/SF ≈ $1.5–3/SF, widened to $2–5/SF for 13R systems. No direct source found; verify locally.

lineItems.notes: Required for townhouses in many IRC/IBC jurisdictions; carve-out of the hard cost.

lineItems.name: Attached/tuck-under garage (2 car)

cost.method: ~400–450 SF unfinished garage at ~50–60% of finished $/SF ($150 mid) ≈ $30k. Judgment; unsourced.

lineItems.notes: Garage SF is not counted in finished SF but is inside the per-unit hard cost.

pctOfHard.method: Same NAHB 2024 for-sale structure as production single-family (A&E, permits/impact/utility fees, financing, builder G&A, marketing ≈ 20% of direct cost). Townhomes add HOA/condo documentation and slightly more engineering (rated assemblies). Mid held at 20%. Commissions are excluded.

softCosts.notes: For build-to-rent townhomes use btr-attached. Impact fees per unit are often charged at the single-family rate.

design.method: Repeatable building types; small design contingency. Judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Low hard $160k × 1.1 ≈ $175k; high $440k × 1.3 ≈ $570k, plus headroom for urban luxury product. Excludes land.

source.title: Issued Residential Building Permits — September 2025, Unincorporated Snohomish County
source.publisher: Snohomish County Planning and Development Services

evidence.quote: $1,925,963 Construction of a 7 unit townhouse development ... for 10,191 square feet. $2,243,044 ... 6 unit townhouse development ... 12,428 square feet. $2,459,017 ... 8 unit ... 13,647 square feet. $3,245,668 ... 10 unit ... 17,596 square feet.
evidence.scopeNotes: Building permit valuations, computed by the researcher: $189, $180, $180 and $184/SF; $275k, $374k, $307k and $325k/unit. Permit valuations usually reflect building construction value from a county table and typically exclude site work, so they are a proxy.

source.title: Cost of Constructing New Homes in Washington State in 2024

evidence.quote: Townhome construction, on average, costs $404 per square foot.
evidence.scopeNotes: Builder survey (NAHB format). BIAW says the figure covers the entire attached structure. The average new townhome was 1,568 SF. Outlier versus the WA single-family figure ($309) and permit valuations; kept as the high spread.

openQuestions: No national cost survey isolates townhomes. NAHB's Cost of Constructing a Home covers detached only. A townhome cost breakdown from a large public builder or a cost consultant would firm this up.
The BIAW $404/SF figure conflicts with WA permit valuations (~$185/SF). Its scope should be checked against the full PDF tables.
